state.case_summary:
A 45-year-old woman presented with a 2-month history of a slowly growing, dull, intermittent swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule. She reported fluctuations in pain intensity and a sensation of heaviness in the area. On examination, teeth #15 and #16 were grossly carious, and there was a firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa. There was no tenderness on percussion of the involved teeth. Panoramic radiography demonstrated a mild periapical radiolucency at the affected root apices. A provisional diagnosis of a periapical abscess was made, and extraction of the carious teeth with socket curettage was planned. Preoperative blood tests (CBC, hemoglobin, blood sugar, bleeding and clotting times) were within normal limits. Under local anesthesia, the teeth were extracted, and curettage yielded a gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue, which was sent for histopathological examination with a provisional diagnosis of periapical granuloma.

C. Periapical granuloma was considered after extraction and curettage yielded tissue presumed to be granulation tissue
D. Sinus inflammation and other odontogenic lesions were also in the differential given the location of the swelling in
